explanations.explanation: I get the thought, friend. A little company sounds nice on a long night. But the text says Jacob sent his family across the stream "along with all his possessions" (Genesis 32:23). Then it says, "So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak." (Genesis 32:24). That makes this one False.

False, and the text is plain about it. Jacob sends his wives, his maidservants, his eleven sons and all his possessions across the stream (Genesis 32:22-23). Then, "So Jacob was left all alone…" (Genesis 32:24). Not one helper stays behind. I can't even hand off a batch without hovering over it.

explanations.answer: He strikes the socket of Jacob's hip
explanations.explanation: That's it. He "struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled" (Genesis 32:25). It comes right after he sees he can't overpower Jacob. And Jacob is still feeling that hip when the sun comes up (Genesis 32:31).

explanations.answer: He shoves Jacob into the stream
explanations.explanation: No dunking in this passage, friend. Jacob's family and everything he owns already crossed the Jabbok before the wrestling starts (Genesis 32:22-23). What the man does is strike "the socket of Jacob’s hip" and dislocate it (Genesis 32:25). The stream stays out of the match, but the hip does not.

explanations.answer: He lets go and slips off into the dark
explanations.explanation: The man doesn't slip away. In verse 26 he says, "Let me go, for it is daybreak." Jacob answers, "I will not let you go unless you bless me." I think I would have let go the second something cracked. I get nervous when a cookie breaks, and this is a HIP.

Israel is right. The man says, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…" (Genesis 32:28). The old name goes out and the new one comes in, right in the middle of the night. Jacob started that night with one name and finished it with another.

Abraham is a name from a different name-change moment. God changed Abram's name to Abraham (Genesis 17:5). It's easy to mix them up, since both are big name moments. Here the man tells Jacob, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…" (Genesis 32:28).

Joshua is a fine name, but it isn't in this passage. The man says, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…" (Genesis 32:28). Joshua is like a sprinkle that wandered into the wrong batch. Nice sprinkle, wrong cookie.

Prevailed is the word. The man says, "…because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed." (Genesis 32:28). Jacob has a dislocated hip and he still gets that word. That's a sentence worth printing on a cookie box.

Fled isn't the word in the verse. Jacob stays put and holds on, telling the man, "I will not let you go unless you bless me." (Genesis 32:26). The man says Jacob has "prevailed" (Genesis 28). If Jacob was running, he had a funny way of showing it.

Lost is a fair guess with a dislocated hip, friend. But the man doesn't say it. He says Jacob has struggled "with God and with men, and you have prevailed." (Genesis 32:28). A sore hip and that word, both in one night.

Blessed is right. "Then he blessed Jacob there." (Genesis 32:29). Back in verse 26 Jacob said he wouldn't let go unless he got a blessing. The man doesn't give his name, but Jacob leaves with the blessing.

Warned isn't in this verse. The man answers with a question, "Why do you ask my name?" Then "he blessed Jacob there." (Genesis 32:29). Jacob had said he wouldn't let go unless he was blessed (Genesis 32:26), and that is what he gets. The man answers a question with a question, and the blessing still shows up.

Thanked would be polite, but the text doesn't say it. After "Why do you ask my name?" the verse says, "Then he blessed Jacob there." (Genesis 32:29). That's the blessing Jacob asked for in verse 26. Nobody in this passage hands out a thank-you note.

explanations.answer: He has seen God face to face and his life was spared
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Jacob gives. He says, "Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared." (Genesis 32:30). So he names the place Peniel. I think a man who says that is still catching his breath.

explanations.answer: He has won the hardest fight of his whole life
explanations.explanation: The man does say Jacob has prevailed (Genesis 32:28), but that isn't the reason Jacob gives for the name. He says, "Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared." (Genesis 32:30). Jacob's words about the place are about God. He doesn't say he won.

explanations.answer: He has finally made peace with his brother Esau
explanations.explanation: At this point Jacob has only heard that Esau is coming to meet him with four hundred men (Genesis 32:6). The reason he gives for Peniel is about God: "Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared." (Genesis 32:30). Esau's part comes later. I'm keeping my mouth shut about it for now.

True. Verse 31 says, "The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip." That's the hip dislocated back in verse 25. Jacob walks into the morning with a limp, friend. That's one way to start the day.

The text says the opposite. "The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip." (Genesis 32:31). The hip dislocated in verse 25 is still with him at sunrise. No spring in his step, only a limp.

explanations.answer: Jacob's hip was struck near that tendon
explanations.explanation: Verse 32 gives the reason itself. The Israelites do not eat that tendon "because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon." When this was written, they still kept it "to this day." A whole habit that goes back to one night by the Jabbok.

explanations.answer: That tendon was set aside for the priests
explanations.explanation: Priests aren't in this verse at all. The text gives its own reason: "because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon." (Genesis 32:32). It's a good guess if you're thinking of what gets set aside. But the reason here is about Jacob's hip.

explanations.answer: That tendon was used to make bowstrings
explanations.explanation: Bowstrings is a creative one, friend. I'd have picked it too if I were guessing in the dark. But the verse says the Israelites do not eat the tendon "because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon." (Genesis 32:32). Nothing in the text mentions bows.
